Step 2 of the [fishing-activity flow](flow.html), for static gear (nets, pots,
longlines). The logbook often records only the haul. The soak starts at the
set, which is then only on the track:
[rb_link_record_sets()](../reference/rb_link_record_sets.html) takes a pass of
the vessel along the haul's line in the hours before it, scored by its lateness
and its length. The rule is that of Ifremer's iapesca package, version 1.3,
recoded. This article measures it on tracks whose pings an observer or an
expert labelled, and compares the variants the function offers.

The other published method is Mendo et al.
([2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolind.2023.110822)), in R in the
article's Supplementary Materials 3 and 4: from hauling pings a classifier
labelled, on a dense track at a regular interval, it takes the vessel's
longest pass through a buffer of the haul that covers most of the haul's
length. It is not recoded in ramb: on these tracks it did no better than
`rb_link_record_sets()` from 2-minute pings on (fishycode decision 234).

```{r}
library(ramb)
library(dplyr)
```

## Labelled tracks

ramb ships three labelled tracks
([rb_read_example()](../reference/rb_read_example.html)). Two have set and haul
labels on static gear: one Italian pot vessel (ICES WKSSFGEO2) and two
Portuguese pot vessels (ICES WKSSFGEO), and four drive-in gillnet fishers in
Madagascar (Behivoke et al., IRD). The pings are a minute apart or closer.

Where Ifremer's iapesca package is installed, its own example vessel is added
(`iapesca::positions`, CC BY 4.0): a passive-gear vessel on 8 trips, a ping every 15
minutes, each labelled setting, hauling or not fishing by iapesca's authors.
It is the one track here at a VMS-like rate. Without the package, the tables
below have no iapesca rows.

```{r}
rd <- function(nm) collect(rb_read_example(nm))
ia <- if (requireNamespace("iapesca", quietly = TRUE)) {
  with(iapesca::positions, tibble(
    vid = as.character(VESSEL_FK),
    time = as.POSIXct(DATE_TIME, tz = "UTC"),
    lon = LONGITUDE,
    lat = LATITUDE,
    op = c(Setting = "set", Hauling = "haul", NotFishing = "other")[as.character(FishingOperation)],
    ds = "iapesca"
  ))
}
p0 <- bind_rows(
  rd("wkssfgeo2_it_pots") |> mutate(ds = "pots"),
  rd("wkssfgeo_pt_gps") |> filter(gear == "pots") |> mutate(ds = "pots"),
  rd("ird_mg_gillnet") |> mutate(ds = "gillnet"),
  ia
) |>
  mutate(vid = as.integer(factor(paste(ds, vid))), op = coalesce(op, "other")) |>
  arrange(vid, time, lon, lat) |>
  distinct(vid, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

A haul is a run of pings labelled hauling, with its first and last position as
the logbook would declare them; a set is a run labelled setting.

```{r}
runs <- function(d, what) {
  d |>
    group_by(vid) |>
    arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    mutate(r = cumsum(op != lag(op, default = "none"))) |>
    filter(op == what) |>
    group_by(ds, vid, r) |>
    summarise(
      start = min(time),
      end = max(time) + 1,
      lon1 = first(lon),
      lat1 = first(lat),
      lon2 = last(lon),
      lat2 = last(lat),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
hauls <- runs(p0, "haul") |> mutate(id = row_number())
sets <- runs(p0, "set")
count(hauls, ds)
```

The true set of a haul is the labelled set run nearest to it in space, ending
before the haul and starting at most 240 hours earlier.

```{r}
truth <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(hauls)), function(i) {
  h <- hauls[i, ]
  hp <- filter(p0, vid == h$vid, time >= h$start, time < h$end)
  cand <- filter(sets, vid == h$vid, end <= h$start, start >= h$start - 240 * 3600)
  if (nrow(cand) == 0) {
    return(tibble(id = h$id, t_s = as.POSIXct(NA), t_e = as.POSIXct(NA)))
  }
  d <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cand)), function(j) {
    sp <- filter(p0, vid == h$vid, time >= cand$start[j], time < cand$end[j])
    g <- expand.grid(a = seq_len(nrow(hp)), b = seq_len(nrow(sp)))
    min(rb_calc_distance(
      lon1 = hp$lon[g$a], lat1 = hp$lat[g$a],
      lon2 = sp$lon[g$b], lat2 = sp$lat[g$b],
      method = "haversine"
    ))
  }, numeric(1))
  j <- which.min(d)
  tibble(id = h$id, t_s = cand$start[j], t_e = cand$end[j])
}) |>
  bind_rows()
hauls |>
  left_join(truth, by = "id") |>
  group_by(ds) |>
  summarise(
    with_a_set = sum(!is.na(t_s)),
    median_soak_h = median(as.numeric(difftime(start, t_e, units = "hours")), na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

The two gears differ the way static gear does: the pots soak for days, the
gillnets for an hour or two, with the fish driven into the net between the set
and the haul. iapesca's vessel leaves its gear for days too.

## The variants, at five ping rates

A found set is right when its pings overlap the true set run. The track is
thinned to one ping per 2, 5, 10 and 30 minutes to see what remains at VMS
rates.

```{r}
thin <- function(p, s) {
  if (s == 0) {
    return(p)
  }
  p |>
    mutate(b = floor(as.numeric(time) / s)) |>
    group_by(vid, b) |>
    slice(1) |>
    ungroup()
}
score <- function(found) {
  x <- hauls |>
    select(id, ds) |>
    left_join(found, by = "id") |>
    left_join(truth, by = "id") |>
    mutate(
      right = !is.na(set_start) & !is.na(t_s) & set_start < t_e & t_s <= set_end,
      wrong = !is.na(set_start) & !is.na(t_s) & !right,
      missed = is.na(set_start) & !is.na(t_s)
    )
  x |>
    group_by(ds) |>
    summarise(cell = sprintf("%d / %d / %d", sum(right), sum(wrong), sum(missed)))
}
variants <- list(
  "as iapesca 1.3 (the defaults)" = list(),
  "the first search alone" = list(consolidate = FALSE),
  "the hour before the haul let in" = list(soak_h = c(0, 240)),
  "the haul's pings as points" = list(method = "pings"),
  "declared positions" = list(method = "record"),
  "line, else declared positions" = list(method = c("line", "record"))
)
h_in <- select(hauls, id, vid, start, end, lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2)
res <- list()
for (s in c(0, 120, 300, 600, 1800)) {
  p <- thin(p0, s) |> select(vid, time, lon, lat)
  for (v in names(variants)) {
    found <- do.call(rb_link_record_sets, c(list(h_in, p, key = "id"), variants[[v]]))
    res[[length(res) + 1]] <- score(found) |>
      mutate(variant = v, rate = if (s == 0) "own" else paste(s / 60, "min"))
  }
}
bind_rows(res) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = rate, values_from = cell) |>
  arrange(ds) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Right / wrong / missed sets per gear, variant and ping rate.")
```

## What the labels say

- **Dense pot tracks: the hour before the haul.** On a track a minute apart,
  the latest pass along the line is the vessel's run in to the buoy. iapesca
  1.3 leaves out the hour before the haul and scores a pass by its length as
  well as its lateness: it finds 33 of the 56 sets, where the rule of
  iapesca's 2022 version, which ramb followed until 2026.10.28, found 13. With
  that hour let in, 16.
- **Drive-in gillnets: the same hour is wrong.** The net is set, the fish
  driven and the net hauled within two hours, so the hour left out holds many
  of the sets: the defaults find 56 of 72, and 70 with the hour let in
  (`soak_h = c(0, 240)`), as the 2022 rule did.
- **Sparse tracks: declared positions.** At 10 and 30 minutes many hauls hold
  fewer than two pings, and the default line, which needs two, misses them.
  The haul's pings as points, or its declared start and end where the logbook
  has them, give a line back: `method = c("line", "record")` misses the
  fewest, though many of the sets it then finds are wrong.
- **iapesca's own vessel: 37 of 39.** At 15 minutes a haul holds a few
  pings. iapesca 1.3's rule finds 37 of its 39 labelled sets, where the 2022
  rule found 19; the second search (`consolidate`) gives 4 of them. Thinning
  to 2, 5 or 10 minutes changes nothing on a track that is already sparser.

The best choice differs by gear and by ping rate. The defaults are iapesca
1.3's (the maintainer, 2026-10-28); each variant is an argument, and
`set_method` says which line each haul was measured against.

## The result on a map

The table counts; a map shows each haul with its labelled set and the set each
variant found. Here are the defaults and the variant that lets in the hour
before the haul, at the tracks' own ping rate, scored as above:

```{r}
p_own <- select(p0, vid, time, lon, lat)
outcome <- function(found) {
  hauls |>
    select(id) |>
    left_join(found, by = "id") |>
    left_join(truth, by = "id") |>
    transmute(
      id, set_start, set_end,
      outcome = case_when(
        is.na(t_s) ~ "no labelled set",
        is.na(set_start) ~ "missed",
        set_start < t_e & t_s <= set_end ~ "right",
        TRUE ~ "wrong"
      )
    )
}
by_default <- outcome(rb_link_record_sets(h_in, p_own, key = "id"))
by_hour <- outcome(rb_link_record_sets(
  h_in, p_own, key = "id", soak_h = c(0, 240)
))
count(by_default, outcome)
count(by_hour, outcome)
```

Each haul, labelled set and found set becomes a line through its pings, in
time order. The vessels lie far apart (Portugal, Madagascar, the Atlantic for
iapesca's vessel, and the Italian vessel's anonymised positions, which fall
inland), so a map shows one vessel, made by a function of the vessel:

```{r}
# a line through the pings of each interval (vid, from, to), with its other columns
lines_of <- function(iv, d) {
  g <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(iv)), function(i) {
    x <- d[d$vid == iv$vid[i] & d$time >= iv$from[i] & d$time <= iv$to[i], ]
    # a pass of one ping (sparse tracks) is a point
    if (nrow(x) == 0) NULL else if (nrow(x) == 1) sf::st_point(c(x$lon, x$lat)) else sf::st_linestring(cbind(x$lon, x$lat))
  })
  keep <- !vapply(g, is.null, logical(1))
  cols <- setdiff(names(iv), c("vid", "from", "to"))
  sf::st_sf(
    as.data.frame(iv)[keep, cols, drop = FALSE],
    geometry = sf::st_sfc(g[keep], crs = 4326)
  )
}

line_layer <- function(id, label, data, colour, visible = TRUE, dash = FALSE, info = NULL) {
  rb_map_layer(
    id, "geojson",
    label = label, info = info, visible = visible, data = data,
    style = list(
      list(
        id = paste0(id, "-line"), type = "line",
        filter = list("==", list("geometry-type"), "LineString"),
        paint = c(
          list("line-color" = colour, "line-width" = 3, "line-opacity" = 0.8),
          if (dash) list("line-dasharray" = list(1, 1))
        )
      ),
      list(
        id = paste0(id, "-dot"), type = "circle",
        filter = list("==", list("geometry-type"), "Point"),
        paint = list("circle-color" = colour, "circle-radius" = 5, "circle-opacity" = 0.8)
      )
    ),
    popup = list(
      click = paste0(id, c("-line", "-dot")), title = "haul",
      fields = list(list(field = "outcome", label = "outcome"))
    )
  )
}

outcome_colour <- list("match", list("get", "outcome"), "right", "#2c5d87", "#d9822b")

sets_map <- function(vessel) {
  d <- filter(p0, vid == .env$vessel)
  h <- filter(hauls, vid == .env$vessel) |>
    left_join(truth, by = "id") |>
    left_join(select(by_default, id, defaults = outcome), by = "id") |>
    left_join(select(by_hour, id, hour = outcome), by = "id")
  found <- function(x) {
    h |>
      select(id, vid) |>
      inner_join(filter(x, !is.na(set_start)), by = "id") |>
      transmute(vid, from = set_start, to = set_end, haul = id, outcome)
  }
  pings <- rb_map_layer(
    "pings", "vector",
    label = "Pings, as labelled",
    tiles = rb_map_tiles_table(
      transmute(d, vid, time, lon, lat, op),
      lon = "lon", lat = "lat", properties = c("vid", "time", "op")
    ),
    count = list(text = "{1} pings"),
    style = list(list(
      id = "pings-dot", type = "circle", "source-layer" = "features",
      paint = list(
        "circle-color" = list("match", list("get", "op"), "set", "#2e8b57", "haul", "#c0392b", "#8a959e"),
        "circle-radius" = list("interpolate", list("linear"), list("zoom"), 10, 1.5, 16, 4)
      )
    )),
    legend = list(
      list(swatch = list(dot = "#2e8b57"), label = "setting"),
      list(swatch = list(dot = "#c0392b"), label = "hauling"),
      list(swatch = list(dot = "#8a959e"), label = "other")
    ),
    popup = list(
      click = "pings-dot", title = "time",
      fields = list(list(field = "vid", label = "vessel"), list(field = "op", label = "label"))
    )
  )
  hauls_layer <- rb_map_layer(
    "hauls", "geojson",
    label = "Hauls",
    data = lines_of(transmute(h, vid, from = start, to = end, haul = id, defaults, hour), d),
    style = list(list(
      id = "hauls-line", type = "line",
      paint = list("line-color" = "#c0392b", "line-width" = 6, "line-opacity" = 0.4)
    )),
    popup = list(
      click = "hauls-line", title = "haul",
      fields = list(
        list(field = "defaults", label = "set found by the defaults"),
        list(field = "hour", label = "set found with the hour before the haul let in")
      )
    )
  )
  labelled <- filter(h, !is.na(t_s)) |>
    transmute(vid, from = t_s, to = t_e, haul = id, outcome = "labelled")
  span <- max(diff(range(d$lon)), 2 * diff(range(d$lat))) # a degree of latitude draws taller
  rb_map(
    rb_map_group("track", "Track", list(
      pings,
      hauls_layer,
      line_layer("truth", "Labelled sets", lines_of(labelled, d), "#2e8b57",
                 dash = TRUE, info = "The labelled set run nearest each haul, the truth above.")
    )),
    rb_map_group("found", "Sets found", list(
      line_layer("defaults", "By the defaults", lines_of(found(by_default), d), outcome_colour,
                 info = "Blue: the found set overlaps the labelled one; orange: it does not."),
      line_layer("hour", "The hour before the haul let in", lines_of(found(by_hour), d), outcome_colour,
                 visible = FALSE, info = "soak_h = c(0, 240).")
    )),
    title = paste("Sets of", d$ds[1], "vessel", vessel),
    view = list(
      center = c(mean(range(d$lon)), mean(range(d$lat))),
      zoom = max(3, min(15, floor(log2(360 / span)) - 1))
    )
  )
}
# the pot vessel and the gillnet fisher with the most hauls
top <- hauls |>
  count(ds, vid) |>
  group_by(ds) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
top
pots_map <- sets_map(top$vid[top$ds == "pots"])
gillnet_map <- sets_map(top$vid[top$ds == "gillnet"])
iapesca_map <- if (any(top$ds == "iapesca")) sets_map(top$vid[top$ds == "iapesca"])
```

The pot vessel is the Italian one, whose positions are anonymised, so its map
opens with no base map:

```{r}
#| eval: false
rb_map_serve(pots_map, query = list(base = "none"))
rb_map_serve(gillnet_map, port = 8791) # beside it, on a port of its own
rb_map_serve(iapesca_map, port = 8792) # where iapesca is installed
# rb_map_stop() when done
```

On the pots map, tick one variant at a time. The defaults' sets lie mostly in
blue on the green labelled sets; with the hour before the haul let in, most
turn orange on the hauls' own lines, the run in to the buoy. On the gillnet map
it goes the other way: the defaults miss or mistake the sets laid within the
hour before the haul, and with that hour let in nearly every set is blue. On
iapesca's map the hauls are a few pings each, and the sets are blue but for
two. A click on a haul gives both outcomes.
